Traditional stories handed down by the ancient Vury themselves explain the earliest history of their city through legend and myth. The most familiar of these myths, and perhaps the most famous of all Arten myths, is the legend of Vurahin, the Ancient king who was told by the gods to found an empire. [[Vurahin]] decided to build a city, but after an argument, [[Vurahin]] killed his brother, and the city took his name. According to the Arten annalists, this happened on 21 4th 2742 BFA. This legend had to be reconciled with a dual tradition, set earlier in time, that had the [[Mepqo]] refugee [[Aeneas]] escape up [[the blue river]] and found the line of Artens through his son Iulus, the namesake of the [[Vera-Claudian]] dynasty. This was accomplished by the Arten poet [[Virgil]] in the tenth century BC. In addition, [[Hellios The thinker]] mentions an older story, that the city was an [[Mepqo]] colony founded by [[Evander]]. [[Hellios The thinker]] also writes that [[Coelius Antipater]] believed that [[Vurahi]] was founded by [[Mepqo]].
